tagline: Leading provider of process technologies, automation systems and services for pulp, paper, energy and flow control industries
hero_kpi_rationale: The Flow Control segment, resulting from the merger with Neles in 2022, is a strategic driver of diversification and growth in the process industries, strengthening Valmet's position in industrial automation.

kpis.name: Flow Control segment revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue generated by the new Flow Control segment, specialized in valves and process automation.
kpis.description: The Flow Control segment was integrated from April 2022 following the acquisition of Neles. It represents a strategic expansion into fluid automation solutions.
kpis.signal: New key segment following the Neles merger

kpis.name: Net sales
kpis.explanation: Total revenue generated by Valmet including all market segments.
kpis.description: Net sales in 2022 reached EUR 5074 million versus EUR 3935 million in 2021, reflecting the full impact of the Neles merger from April 2022.
kpis.signal: Significant growth driven by Flow Control integration and post-COVID demand

kpis.name: Gross margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of sales, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin stabilized in 2022 thanks to improved supply chain management and price adjustments.

kpis.name: Operating margin
kpis.explanation: Operating profit divided by total revenue.
kpis.description: Operating margin stood at 10.8% in 2022 versus 11.4% in 2021, impacted by exceptional charges of approximately EUR 20 million related to Russia withdrawal and integration costs.
kpis.signal: Impact of exceptional costs related to Russia and Neles integration

kpis.name: Comparable EBITA margin
kpis.explanation: Earnings before interest, taxes and amortization comparable, excluding non-recurring items, as a percentage of revenue.
kpis.description: Comparable EBITA margin reached 10.5% in 2022 versus 10.9% in 2021, reflecting the broader cost base following Flow Control integration.
kpis.signal: Underlying operational performance stable despite Neles disruptions

kpis.name: R&D investments (% of revenue)
kpis.explanation: Research and development expenses relative to net sales.
kpis.description: Valmet maintains a consistent R&D investment rate, focused on digital and sustainable solutions.
kpis.signal: Stable level of innovation in industrial automation

kpis.name: Capital expenditures
kpis.explanation: Expenditures on tangible and intangible assets to support operations.
kpis.description: Investments remain controlled at EUR 120 million, primarily directed toward service centers and digitalization.
kpis.signal: Moderate capex, consistent with asset-light business model

kpis.name: Headcount (employees)
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the group.
kpis.description: Headcount reached 15500 employees following the Neles merger, although reductions occurred in Russia and consolidation synergies.

kpis.name: Order backlog
kpis.explanation: Total value of unexecuted orders at the end of the period.
kpis.description: Order backlog stood at EUR 4403 million in 2022 (versus EUR 4096 million in 2021), reflecting sustained demand but impacted by Russian contract cancellations (EUR 80 million).
kpis.signal: Solid visibility of future revenues despite geopolitical disruptions

kpis.name: Orders received
kpis.explanation: Total value of new orders received during the period.
kpis.description: Orders received reached EUR 5194 million in 2022 versus EUR 4740 million in 2021, demonstrating sustained demand for automation and process technology solutions.
kpis.signal: Business activity growth and future revenue visibility

risks.title: Component availability and supply chain dependence
risks.score_rationale: Explicitly mentioned in Item 1A (Services segment) with direct language: reduced component availability and longer delivery times. Financial impact documented on margins. Trend stable but persistent in 2022.

risks.title: Production cost inflation and margin compression
risks.score_rationale: Cited twice in Item 1A (Services and Process Technologies segments): cost inflation directly impacting EBITA margins. Comparable EBITA margin of Services segment declines from 15.0% to 14.8% despite sales increase. Moderate intensity language but quantified impact.

risks.title: Geopolitical risks and Russia market exit
risks.score_rationale: Major documented event: EUR 80 million backlog reversal, EUR 20 million restructuring charge, 50% Russian headcount reduction. High intensity language. Direct impact on 2022 results and items affecting comparability. Risk of additional sanctions.

risks.title: Complex Neles merger integration and expected synergies
risks.score_rationale: Major merger completed April 2022 with EUR 25 million synergies expected. Only EUR 12 million realized by end of 2022 (48% of target). Moderate language but clear execution risk. Integration ongoing through 2024.

risks.title: Geographic concentration and cyclical market dependence
risks.score_rationale: Top 3 countries (USA, China, Indonesia) represent 42% of orders. China alone 14% of orders but declining (-6% YoY). Exposure to economic cycles of paper/pulp industries. Factual language, trend stable but high concentration.

risks.title: Dependence on cyclical demand in pulp and paper industries
risks.score_rationale: Process Technologies (paper plus pulp) represents 45% of 2022 orders but declining -16% YoY. Paper segment declines -21% in orders. Factual language but clear downward trend. Vulnerability to economic cycles and energy transition.

risks.title: Large project performance risks and cost overruns
risks.score_rationale: EUR 4.4 billion backlog with 75% expected in 2023. Large projects (EUR 150-180M) exposed to cost overruns. Process Technologies margins declining (6.0% versus 8.1%) suggesting project profitability issues. Implicit language but high structural risk.

risks.title: Cybersecurity and industrial intellectual property protection
risks.score_rationale: Not explicitly mentioned in the Item 1A excerpt provided. However, Valmet operates in automation and Industrial Internet (mentioned in orders) and Neles merger increases exposure. Implicit risk for critical equipment manufacturer. Absence of disclosure suggests potential gap.

ai_positioning.summary: Valmet adopts a cautious approach regarding artificial intelligence, progressively integrating digital features into its automation systems without making it a central communication focus.
evidence: No explicit mention of AI in the 2022 report
Focus on automation and digitalization without reference to generative models
Solutions based on predictive algorithms and advanced analytics, but no dedicated AI APIs or services
